canonical_statement: The study compared cardiovascular outcome risks between new users of dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a broad Korean population with type 2 diabetes.
The study was a nationwide population-based cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance Service and health-screening data.
The investigators applied an active-comparator, new-user design to dapagliflozin and empagliflozin initiators.
Death records from Statistics Korea were merged with NHIS data so that cardiovascular death outcomes could be ascertained.
The study followed the STROBE reporting guideline.
Eligible patients had type 2 diabetes and initiated an SGLT2 inhibitor between May 2016 and December 2018.

Empagliflozin initiation was the active comparator.
The primary outcome was a composite of heart-failure-related events, ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and cardiovascular death.

outcome.definition: Composite of heart-failure-related events (hospitalization or heart-failure death), ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and cardiovascular death

canonical_statement: Heart-failure-related event was defined as Hospitalization for heart failure or death from heart failure.

outcome.definition: Hospitalization for heart failure or death from heart failure

canonical_statement: Ischemic stroke was defined as Hospital admission with ICD-10 I63 or I64 plus a brain CT or MRI claim.

outcome.definition: Hospital admission with ICD-10 I63 or I64 plus a brain CT or MRI claim

canonical_statement: Myocardial infarction was defined as Hospital admission with ICD-10 I21 or I22 plus CABG or coronary angiography procedure code.

outcome.definition: Hospital admission with ICD-10 I21 or I22 plus CABG or coronary angiography procedure code

canonical_statement: Cardiovascular death was defined as Death with cardiovascular cause code I000–I999.

outcome.definition: Death with cardiovascular cause code I000–I999

canonical_statement: End-stage renal disease was prespecified as a safety outcome.
Diabetic ketoacidosis was prespecified as a safety outcome.
Genitourinary tract infection was prespecified as a safety outcome.
Hypoglycemia was prespecified as a safety outcome.
Propensity scores were estimated with logistic regression using index year and 48 clinically relevant covariates, followed by 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching without replacement.
Absolute standardized differences were used to assess balance; values under 10% were prespecified as balanced, and all matched baseline characteristics had absolute standardized differences below 5%.
Patients were followed from the index date until the primary outcome, death, or December 2019; emigration was treated as censoring.
Incidence rates were expressed per 1,000 person-years, Kaplan–Meier curves were compared by log-rank test, and Cox regression estimated hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals.
Sensitivity analyses included prespecified subgroup analyses, an as-treated analysis censoring medication gaps longer than 28 days, and comparison of non-cardiovascular mortality.
Dapagliflozin was not significantly associated with a different risk of the primary composite outcome versus empagliflozin (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.855–1.006; p=0.07).

Genitourinary tract infection risk did not differ significantly between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin users (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.984–1.031; p=0.534).

Among women, dapagliflozin was associated with a lower primary-composite risk versus empagliflozin (adjusted HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.738–0.968); the sex interaction p-value was 0.044.

canonical_statement: The source is internally inconsistent about the lower bound of the primary-outcome 95% CI: the abstract and main Results text report 0.855, while Figure 2 prints 0.858; the upper bound is 1.006 in both locations.
The authors concluded that composite cardiovascular outcomes did not differ significantly between new users of dapagliflozin and empagliflozin.

The authors concluded that dapagliflozin might be associated with lower risks of heart-failure hospitalization or death and cardiovascular death than empagliflozin in Asian patients with type 2 diabetes.
Potential residual confounding remained despite adjustment; aspirin and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor use were not available.
The cohort consisted mainly of Korean patients, limiting generalizability to other racial and ethnic populations.
Dosage information for dapagliflozin and empagliflozin was unavailable.
Treatment adherence could not be confirmed, although intention-to-treat and as-treated analyses produced similar overall findings.
The Seoul National University Hospital institutional review board exempted the study protocol from review (IRB 2003-006-1105) because the NHIS data were anonymized and de-identified.
